Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Automotive Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Automotive's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Sarah Patel, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Lisa Moreno, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Reflecting on Q2, we are proud of the significant strides NovaVolt Automotive has made across all facets of our business. We have achieved remarkable progress in capital expenditure plans and investment priorities, production volume and capacity utilization rates, gross margin percentage and trends, battery costs per kWh and trends, strategic outlook and priorities for the next quarter and year, delivery volume guidance by model, factory expansions and operational efficiency improvements, and changes in order backlog and reservation trends. The market reception to our NovaVolt One SUV has been overwhelmingly positive, with the associated impact of product far exceeding our initial estimates.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to discuss our financial performance in greater detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Elena, and good morning, everyone. Our revenue for Q2 reached $2.8 billion, marking an exceptional 45% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin expanded to 19.2%, driven by enhanced operational efficiencies and a favorable product mix. Operating expenses amounted to $850 million, resulting in a net income of $320 million. Our financial position remains strong, with $5.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We anticipate revenue of $3.1 to $3.4 billion for the upcoming quarter.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here on the West Coast. As we dive deeper into our operational metrics, I'd like to focus on production volume and capacity utilization rates, which remain the cornerstone of our path to sustainable profitability in this hyper-competitive EV landscape. Our team has executed aggressively against our ramp targets, navigating supply chain headwinds from battery cell shortages and semiconductor constraints that have plagued the industry—think the ongoing ripple effects from TSMC's Taiwan disruptions and CATL's raw material squeezes.

In Q2, we delivered total production volume of 285,000 vehicles, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase and a 12% sequential improvement from Q1's 254,000 units. This puts us on track for our full-year guidance of 1.2 million vehicles, a 35% uplift from 2023's 890,000. Breaking it down by model lineup: Our flagship NovaVolt One SUV, our volume leader akin to Tesla's Model Y, accounted for 62% of output at 177,000 units. Production here surged 35% YoY, driven by the Nevada Gigafactory 2.0 ramp, where we're now churning out optimized structural battery packs with our in-house 46-series cells—a direct response to LFP cathode price volatility.

The NovaVolt Pro sedan, targeting the premium segment against the BMW i4 and Polestar 2, hit 68,000 units, up 22% YoY, with efficiencies gained from die-casting megacasts that reduced body-in-white cycle times by 18% to under 45 seconds per unit. Newer platforms like the NovaVolt Lite pickup—our Cybertruck challenger—contributed 40,000 units, a 150% QoQ jump as we scale from job-one in March. This model's gigacast exoskeleton is yielding 25% material cost savings, but we're still ironing out stainless steel forming tolerances.

On capacity utilization, we achieved an average of 78% across our global footprint, up from 65% in Q2 2023 and 72% in Q1 2024. This reflects disciplined capex allocation and our 'utilization-first' philosophy amid softening demand signals in Europe. North America—Fremont and Texas Gigafactories—at 42% of total capacity with a 1.0 million annualized run-rate, utilized at 72%. Fremont hit 82% on NovaVolt One lines, benefiting from IRA Section 45X credits that boosted effective cell margins by 15%. Texas Gigafactory, post its Phase 2 expansion, is ramping to 500,000 units/year for pickups; Q2 utilization was 55%, but we're projecting 75% by Q4 via automated kitting stations that cut downstream logistics by 30%.

Asia-Pacific—Shanghai Gigafactory—at 35% of capacity with an 800,000 annualized rate, running hot at 92% utilization—our crown jewel. Export volumes to Europe and APAC offset China's domestic price wars from BYD and NIO, with NovaVolt One exports up 40% YoY. We've localized 85% of our LFP supply chain here, mitigating U.S. tariffs on Chinese cells. Europe—Berlin-Brandenburg Gigafactory—at 23% of capacity with 500,000 annualized, at 68% utilization. Challenges persist from EU CBAM carbon border taxes and slower demand cannibalization, but our NovaVolt Pro right-hand-drive variant for the UK added 12,000 units. We're deploying 800kW ultra-fast chargers on-site to support 24/7 shifts.

Key technical initiatives include vertical battery integration—40% of Q2 cells from our JV with Panasonic at Texas, transitioning to 4680 dry-electrode formats, slashing rejection rates from 8% to 3.2%, unlocking 15% more throughput per line. AI-driven manufacturing with Oracle MICROS integration with Siemens PLCs for predictive maintenance reduced unplanned downtime by 22%, targeting sub-1% scrap rates. Our 'UniBody 2.0' architecture shares 70% components across models, enabling flexible line swaps—critical as we prep the $25k NovaVolt Nano compact for H1 2025 launch to counter mass-market blitzes.

Strategically, these metrics position us ahead of peers. While others idle at lower utilization amid voucher cliffs, our 78% average signals operating leverage—gross margins expanded 420bps to 19.2%. Forward-looking, we're guiding Q3 production to 310,000 units at 82% utilization, with $2.2 billion capex focused on Texas Phase 3 and a new India plant.

Turning to gross margin percentage and trends, which continues to be a cornerstone of our path to sustained profitability. In Q2 2024, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 19.2%, marking a 340 basis point sequential improvement from Q1 and a robust 620 basis point year-over-year expansion from last year. Excluding one-time IRA credits worth about 120 basis points, our adjusted gross margin still came in at 18.1%, underscoring genuine underlying progress.

Our gross margins have followed a classic J-curve recovery: Q2 2023 at 12.5%, Q3 13.9%, Q4 14.8%, Q1 2024 15.3%, and Q2 18.7% headline. This reflects cost discipline, product mix optimization, and regional tailwinds. COGS per vehicle fell 22% YoY to around $41,000, driven by a 28% plunge in battery pack pricing—BloombergNEF reports average kWh costs dropping to $112 globally. We've locked in multi-year offtake with CATL and Panasonic at $85/kWh for 800V architectures. In-house structural packs at Nevada Gigafactory #2 account for 65% of NovaVolt One volume, shaving $3,200 per pack. Gigacasting reduced part count by 40% and assembly time by 25%, boosting labor productivity to 85 vehicles per line per day.

Favorable mix contributed 250 basis points: NovaVolt One SUV at 58% of deliveries with $68,500 ASP versus $52,000 for base models. Software attach rates at 72% for our Level 2+ autonomy stack add $1,800 high-margin revenue. North America at 21.2% margins bolstered by IRA credits and tariffs; Europe at 15.4% navigating subsidy phase-outs but stabilized by localization; China JV at 16.8%.

Key initiatives: 4680 tabless cells by Q4 targeting $70/kWh; 95% NA localization by 2025; factory utilization at 82% for 5-7% quarterly accretion. We guide Q3 adjusted gross margins to 20-21%, full-year 19%, expanding to 25%+ in 2025.

I'll now turn to our capital expenditure plans and investment priorities, which remain the cornerstone of our strategy to scale production, drive technological leadership, and capture market share in the fast-evolving EV landscape. The automotive industry is undergoing its most profound transformation since the shift from horse to horsepower, fueled by electrification, autonomy, and supply chain re-shoring. With global EV sales projected to hit 17 million units in 2024 per BloombergNEF—up 20% YoY—we're positioning NovaVolt to outpace peers.

For fiscal 2024, we're guiding CapEx to $5.8 to $6.2 billion, a 25% increase from 2023. Looking to 2025-2027, cumulative CapEx of $18-20 billion, maintaining a 12-15% CapEx-to-revenue ratio. Breakdown: 45% manufacturing capacity expansion, 30% R&D and advanced technology, 15% supply chain and vertical integration, 10% network infrastructure.

Manufacturing capacity expansion—$2.7B in 2024: Scaling Nevada Gigafactory 2.0 to 500,000 vehicles/year by Q4 2025 with Industry 4.0 automation and 95% uptime via AI predictive maintenance. North America: $700 million for 100 GWh Kentucky cell plant leveraging IRA credits for LFP cathodes, reducing costs 15-20%. Europe: €400 million for Berlin to 150,000 units/year, compliant with EU mandates. Asia-Pacific: $200 million India JV for 50 GWh. Total capacity to 1.2 million by 2026 with cell-to-pack integration.

R&D—$1.8B: $900 million next-gen batteries including solid-state prototypes at 800 Wh/kg partnering innovators for 10,000 units H2 2025. $300 million 800V platforms for 10-minute charging; $200 million Level 4 autonomy with NVIDIA Orin-X and LiDAR; $100 million SiC inverters boosting efficiency to 97%.

Supply chain—$900M: $500 million U.S. pCAM via Panasonic JV for 70% domestic sourcing; $200 million silicon-dominant anodes; $200 million Texas rare earth magnets reducing China reliance.

Charging ecosystem—$600M: $300 million NovaVolt Superhub to 5,000 stalls NACS-compatible; $200 million V2G pilots.

These align with cost leadership to $80/kWh by 2026, premium differentiation, geographic diversification. Expect 3x ROIC over five years with $1.2B IRA tailwinds. Risks mitigated by 20% deferrable CapEx and $2B dry powder.

Before I hand off, a quick note on battery costs per kWh and trends—one of the most critical drivers of EV profitability. Batteries represent 35-40% of BOM. In Q2, average pack cost at $92/kWh, 30% YoY decline from $132/kWh, 12% sequential from Q1. NMC at $105/kWh down 25%, LFP at $75/kWh down 35%. Ahead of industry average $139/kWh, on par with peers at $90-100/kWh.

Trends: 15-20% CAGR decline per McKinsey; scale to 5 TWh capacity by 2025 with 20% discounts locked in. Dry electrode for 40% capex reduction; cell-to-pack at 750 Wh/L. Chemistry shifts to LFP and silicon anodes. Regional: China $56-65/kWh, NA $110 netting $65 post-credits, Europe $120-130. $2.5B to 100 GWh in-house by 2027; recycling recovers 95% materials. Risks hedged 70%.

On delivery volume guidance by model for Q4 2024 and FY2025: Q4 total 35,000-40,000 units, FY24 125,000-130,000. NovaX Compact SUV 22,000-25,000 (55-60% mix), NA 65%; VoltStream Sedan 7,500-9,000 (20-25%); ThunderVolt Pickup 5,500-6,000 (15-20%). FY25 NovaX 200,000+, premium mix up.

Changes in order backlog and reservation trends: Backlog $18.7 billion, 22% YoY up, 285,000 units at $65,500 ASP—18 months visibility. Reservations 142,000 up 15% QoQ for CyberForge and Aether. NA 72%, Europe 18% up 45%, APAC 7%. Premium pivot 84% backlog. Guide $22-25B by year-end.

Next, we'll hear from Sarah regarding the latest developments in our manufacturing operations.

Sarah Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at optimal levels to meet the surging demand for our vehicles. We have successfully implemented advanced automation technologies, resulting in increased production output and reduced cycle times.

As we dive into operational highlights, let's focus on factory expansions and operational efficiency improvements transforming our cost structure. Factory expansions represent $4.2 billion FY24 capex, scaling 65% to 1.2 million units by end-2025. NA: Spartanburg Gigafactory 500,000 units/year with $1.1B IRA credits, 80% domestic content. Europe: Köl n +40%, Debrecen 20 GWh. APAC: Shanghai to 400,000, Chennai 150,000. Modular "factory-in-a-box" cuts build times 35%.

Efficiency via NovaVolt Lean 2.0: Cobotic automation OEE to 94%, AI VoltAI scrap to 0.8%, battery yields 95% at $95/kWh. Supply chain turns 12.5x, 85% renewables, energy intensity down 19%.

These cement cost leadership to $80/kWh by 2026.

Following me, Dr. Singh will provide an update on our technological innovations.

Dr. Raj Singh:
Thank you. Our R&D team is relentlessly pursuing breakthroughs in battery technology, autonomous driving systems, and vehicle connectivity. We are committed to delivering cutting-edge solutions that will redefine the future of mobility. This includes next-gen solid-state batteries targeting 800 Wh/kg and 1,000-mile range, 800V architectures for 10-minute charging, Level 4 autonomy with NVIDIA Orin-X and LiDAR for 99.9% disengagement-free miles, and SiC inverters at 97% efficiency—supporting 20% R&D-to-revenue and 15-20% margin expansion.

After me, Lisa will offer insights into our supply chain strategies.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you. We have established a resilient and diversified supply chain network to mitigate risks and ensure the seamless flow of materials. Our proactive approach has enabled us to navigate global challenges effectively, with 70% domestic sourcing by 2026, backward integration on rare earths, and hedging against metal volatility amid U.S.-China decoupling and Red Sea disruptions.

Next, Tom will share updates on our sales performance and market expansion initiatives.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you. Our sales team has achieved remarkable success in expanding our market reach and driving revenue growth. We are seeing strong demand for our vehicles across all regions, and we are actively pursuing new market opportunities, with NA leveraging IRA for 25% SUV share, Europe countering tariffs via localization, and APAC scaling JVs.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one.

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On capex priorities, can you elaborate on the ROIC expectations and how flexible the plan is amid demand uncertainty?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question. Our capex blueprint expects a 3x return over five years, driven by scale and IRA tailwinds totaling $1.2B through 2028. We've built in 20% deferrable portions for flexibility, plus $2B dry powder for M&A opportunities like distressed suppliers.

Analyst 2:
Great, follow-up for Michael: With gross margins at 19.2%, what's the biggest driver for Q3 guidance to 20-21%, and any color on regional variances?

Michael Chen:
Sure. The biggest drivers are battery deflation to $92/kWh and utilization to 82%, adding 5-7% accretion per 10% volume. NA at 21%+ with credits; Europe stabilizing at 16% post-localization.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Sarah, on production ramp, how are you addressing stainless steel tolerances on the Lite pickup, and Q3 utilization outlook?

Sarah Patel:
We're optimizing forming processes with AI vision, reducing tolerances to spec, similar to peer pilots. Q3 at 82% average, Texas to 75% with kitting automation cutting logistics 30%.

Analyst 4:
Raj, for the CTO: Details on Level 4 autonomy timeline and how it ties to solid-state battery pilots?

Dr. Raj Singh:
Level 4 stack with Orin-X and LiDAR targets 99.9% highway disengagements by 2026, with OTA updates. Solid-state prototypes partner with innovators for 10,000 units H2 2025 at 800 Wh/kg, addressing range anxiety per J.D. Power.

Analyst 5:
Lisa, supply chain: With nickel volatility, what's your hedging coverage and diversification progress?

Lisa Moreno:
Hedged 70% through 2025, diversifying to synthetic graphite JVs in U.S. and pCAM production via Panasonic for 70% domestic lithium/nickel/cobalt by 2026.

Analyst 6:
Tom, sales: Reservation trends for new models—any pull-forward from FSD betas?

Tom Reilly:
Reservations up 15% QoQ to 142,000, with 12% conversion lift from OTA FSD betas. CyberForge Launch Edition sold out through Q2 2025.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 7:
Elena, strategic outlook for FY25—revenue guide and EBITDA margins?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
FY25 revenue $28-30 billion, 650,000 vehicles, 45% growth to 4.5% global share. EBITDA to 12%, up from 8%, with opex down 8% of revenue, software at 75% margins on 2M subscribers.

Analyst 8:
Michael, on backlog: $18.7B is strong, but APAC softness—any Q4 catalysts?

Michael Chen:
APAC 7% but bright spots in Australia/Japan. Q4 catalysts: Shanghai JV LFP for China entry, CyberForge launch pulling $2-3B fulfillment.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Dr. Vasquez for closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We're confident in our ability to continue delivering exceptional results and creating long-term value for our shareholders—scaling efficiently with $92/kWh batteries today to $65/kWh by 2026, 25%+ margins, FCF positive. We look forward to sharing our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Automotive Q2 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
